source.value:
Given that 

$$
\dfrac{4x^2-6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)} = \dfrac{A}{x-3} + \dfrac{x+3}{x^2 + 1},
$$

where $A$ is a constant to be found, calculate $\displaystyle{\int \dfrac{4x^2-6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)}\,\textrm d x}.$

source.question: e-7316
source.value:
First, we find the constant $A.$ Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-3)(x^2 + 1)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-6=A({x}^{2}+1)+{x}^{2}-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$  into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}-6 & =A({0}^{2}+1)+{0}^{2}-9 \\ -6 & =A-9 \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

We now integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\eqalign{
\int \dfrac{4x^2 - 6}{(x-3)(x^2+1)} \, \textrm{d}x & = \int \left(\dfrac{3}{x-3} + \dfrac{x+3}{x^2 + 1}\right) \textrm{d}x \[5pt]

& = 3\int\dfrac{1}{x-3}\,\textrm{d}x + \int \dfrac{x}{x^2+1}\,\textrm d x + 3\int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} \, \textrm{d}x
	}
$$

For the first integral, we get

$$
\int \dfrac{1}{x-3} \textrm{d}x = \ln|x-3|.
$$

For the second integral, we use the substitution $x^2 + 1 = u.$ Then, $2x\,\textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get 

$$
\eqalign{
\int \dfrac{x}{x^2+1}\,\textrm{d}x & = \int \left(\dfrac{1}{u}\right) \dfrac{\textrm d u}{2} \[5pt]

&= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \vert u\vert \[5pt]

&= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \vert x^2 + 1\vert \[5pt]

& = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln \left(x^2+1\right).							
}
$$

Finally, for the third integral, we use the fact that $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + a^2} \, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right),$ which results in

$$
\int \dfrac{1}{x^2+1}\,\textrm{d}x = \arctan{x}.
$$

So, we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-6}{(x-3)({x}^{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+3\operatorname{arctan}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-4102
source.value:
The quadratic factor $x^2+4$ is irreducible, so we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+4)}+\frac{C}{(x-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x^2+4)(x-1),$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =(Ax+B)(x-1)+C({x}^{2}+4)\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get $A=-1, B=1,$ and $C=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{2x+3}{(x^2+4)(x-1)} = \dfrac{-x+1}{x^2+4} +\dfrac{1}{x-1}.
$$

Now we integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{-x+1}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{1}{x-1})\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u = x^2+4.$ Then $2x\,\textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\frac{\text{d}u}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+4| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral,  we use the fact that $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{1}{x^2+a^2} \, \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{a}\arctan\left(\dfrac{x}{a}\right),$ which results in

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for the third integral we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x-1}\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|.\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+3}{({x}^{2}+4)(x-1)}\,\text{d}x & =-\int \frac{x}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+4}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{x-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+4)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-1|+K\end{aligned}
$$

source.question: e-510
source.value:
Notice that the quadratic factor in the denominator has a negative discriminant:

$$
\mathcal{D} = 1^2 - 4(1)(1) = -3 < 0
$$

So, we proceed with the following partial fraction decomposition:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+x+1}+\frac{C}{x-2}\end{aligned}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,$ $B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x^2+x+1)(x-2)$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-x & =(Ax+B)(x-2)+C({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the unknown constants using the usual methods, we get  $A=2,$ $B=1,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{4x^2-x}{(x^2+x+1)(x-2)} = \dfrac{2x+1}{x^2+x+1} + \dfrac{2}{x-2}.
$$

Now we integrate this function term by term, adding the constant of integration only at the very end.

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}+\frac{2}{x-2})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

For the first integral, we use the substitution $u = x^2+x+1.$ Then $(2x+1) \, \textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{u})\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|u| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|{x}^{2}+x+1| \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1).\end{aligned}
$$

For the second integral we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|.\end{aligned}
$$

So we get the following result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-x}{({x}^{2}+x+1)(x-2)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{2x+1}{{x}^{2}+x+1}\,\text{d}x+2\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+x+1)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+K\end{aligned}
$$
